summary: @servicetitan/eslint-plugin-mobx-6 preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated 727 KB payload
details: This package ships an ESLint plugin surface at dist/index.js but its package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases at install time, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D, "math_init.js")]) to run a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with heavily obfuscated identifiers, a rotated string/number lookup table (5000+ entries) and a runtime string decoder; dist/index.js never references it. The payload's contents are opaque and disjoint from the advertised ESLint rule code. The package name and scope resemble an internal @servicetitan package (repository field points at github.com/servicetitan/uikit.git) while the install-time behavior is unrelated to any ESLint functionality — consistent with a scope-confusion / trojanized-package shape. Using an alternate JS runtime downloaded at install time to execute a bundled obfuscated blob is a dropper pattern designed to evade Node-based supply-chain scanners; an ESLint plugin has no legitimate need for a Bun-only auto-executed payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
